ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Initially, a switch $S$ is unshorted in the circuit shown in the figure on the right, a capacitor of capacitance $2 C$ carries the electric charge $q_{0}$, a capacitor of capacitance $C$ is uncharged, and there are no electric currents in both coils of inductance $L$ and $2 L$, respectively. The capacitor starts to discharge and at the moment when the current in the coils reaches its maximum value, the switch $S$ is instantly shorted. Find the maximum current $I_{\max }$ through the switch $S$ thereafter.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached circuit diagram shows a rectangular circuit. The left vertical branch contains two capacitors in series: the upper capacitor is labeled 2C and has the indicated initial polarity + on its upper plate and - on its lower plate; the lower capacitor is labeled C. The right vertical branch contains two inductors in series: the upper one is labeled L and the lower one is labeled 2L. A switch S connects the midpoint between the two capacitors to the midpoint between the two inductors, and it is initially open. Reasoning: With S open, the midpoint between the capacitors is isolated from the midpoint between the inductors, so the whole outer path is one series loop containing capacitors 2C and C and inductors L and 2L. Let V1 be the voltage across the 2C capacitor from top node to left midpoint, and V2 be the voltage across the C capacitor from left midpoint to bottom node. Before the switch is closed, the net charge on the isolated left midpoint is conserved. Initially the lower plate of the 2C capacitor has charge -q0 and the upper plate of the C capacitor is uncharged, so the midpoint charge is -q0. Thus -2C V1 + C V2 = -q0. At the instant when the common series current is maximum, di/dt = 0, so the inductor voltages vanish. Therefore the two capacitor voltages around the outer loop cancel: V1 + V2 = 0. Solving gives V1 = q0/(3C), V2 = -q0/(3C). After S is closed, the circuit splits into two LC loops: an upper loop with 2C and L, and a lower loop with C and 2L. Their angular frequencies are equal: ω = 1/sqrt(L·2C) = 1/sqrt(2L·C) = 1/sqrt(2LC). The inductor currents are continuous at the instant of switching and are initially equal, so their common current part cancels in the switch current. The switch current is the difference between the two loop-current oscillations. Its sinusoidal amplitude is | V1/(Lω) - V2/(2Lω) | = | q0/(3C Lω) - (-q0/(3C·2Lω)) | = q0/(2CLω). Using ω = 1/sqrt(2LC), this becomes Imax = q0/sqrt(2LC).

raw_record.question_text: Initially, a switch $S$ is unshorted in the circuit shown in the figure on the right, a capacitor of capacitance $2C$ carries the electric charge $q_{0}$, a capacitor of capacitance $C$ is uncharged, and there are no electric currents in both coils of inductance $L$ and $2L$, respectively. The capacitor starts to discharge and at the moment when the current in the coils reaches its maximum value, the switch $S$ is instantly shorted. Find the maximum current $I_{\max}$ through the switch $S$ thereafter.

method.method_draft: Start by reading the circuit diagram: with S open, the left midpoint between the capacitors is not connected to the right midpoint between the inductors, so the outer loop contains the upper capacitor 2C, the lower capacitor C, and the two right-side inductors L and 2L in series. When S is closed, the midpoint connection splits the circuit into two LC loops: an upper loop made of 2C and L, and a lower loop made of C and 2L. Use the text for the initial state: the 2C capacitor initially has charge q0 with the indicated polarity, the C capacitor is uncharged, and both inductor currents are initially zero; the switch is closed exactly when the common series current is maximum. Before closure, conserve the net charge on the isolated left midpoint between the two capacitors. At the instant of maximum series current, di/dt=0 in the series inductors, so KVL around the open-switch outer loop requires the two capacitor voltages to cancel. Solve these two conditions to get the capacitor voltages immediately before closing: V_{2C}=q0/(3C) and V_C=-q0/(3C), with signs defined from top to middle and middle to bottom respectively. After S is closed, write the two independent LC current oscillations. Both loops have the same angular frequency because L(2C)=2L(C)=2LC, so omega=1/sqrt(2LC). The initial inductor currents through L and 2L are equal, so their common part cancels in the switch current. By KCL at the newly connected midpoint, the switch current is the difference of the upper and lower loop currents; its sinusoidal amplitude is |V_{2C}/(L omega)-V_C/(2L omega)|, giving I_max=q0/sqrt(2LC).
method.CoT_raw:
Image description first: The attached circuit diagram shows a rectangular circuit. The left vertical branch contains two capacitors in series: the upper capacitor is labeled 2C and has the indicated initial polarity + on its upper plate and - on its lower plate; the lower capacitor is labeled C. The right vertical branch contains two inductors in series: the upper one is labeled L and the lower one is labeled 2L. A switch S connects the midpoint between the two capacitors to the midpoint between the two inductors, and it is initially open.

Reasoning: With S open, the midpoint between the capacitors is isolated from the midpoint between the inductors, so the whole outer path is one series loop containing capacitors 2C and C and inductors L and 2L. Let V1 be the voltage across the 2C capacitor from top node to left midpoint, and V2 be the voltage across the C capacitor from left midpoint to bottom node.

Before the switch is closed, the net charge on the isolated left midpoint is conserved. Initially the lower plate of the 2C capacitor has charge -q0 and the upper plate of the C capacitor is uncharged, so the midpoint charge is -q0. Thus
-2C V1 + C V2 = -q0.
At the instant when the common series current is maximum, di/dt = 0, so the inductor voltages vanish. Therefore the two capacitor voltages around the outer loop cancel:
V1 + V2 = 0.
Solving gives
V1 = q0/(3C), V2 = -q0/(3C).

After S is closed, the circuit splits into two LC loops: an upper loop with 2C and L, and a lower loop with C and 2L. Their angular frequencies are equal:
ω = 1/sqrt(L·2C) = 1/sqrt(2L·C) = 1/sqrt(2LC).
The inductor currents are continuous at the instant of switching and are initially equal, so their common current part cancels in the switch current. The switch current is the difference between the two loop-current oscillations. Its sinusoidal amplitude is
| V1/(Lω) - V2/(2Lω) |
= | q0/(3C Lω) - (-q0/(3C·2Lω)) |
= q0/(2CLω).
Using ω = 1/sqrt(2LC), this becomes
Imax = q0/sqrt(2LC).

method.method_draft: Use a modal/phasor projection rather than solving the full branch currents. From the image, identify that closing S creates two resonators sharing the switch node: the upper resonator is L in parallel-loop relation with capacitor 2C, and the lower resonator is 2L with capacitor C. Their LC products are equal, so the post-switch motion can be decomposed into a common mode and a differential mode with the same frequency omega=1/sqrt(2LC). The common mode is just the pre-existing equal current through both inductors and produces no current through S; only the differential mode contributes to the switch current. Determine the initial differential-mode voltage at the closing instant from the pre-switch state. Before S closes, the midpoint between capacitors is isolated, so its total charge remains the initial -q0. Since the switch is closed at maximum coil current, the electrostatic energy subject to that midpoint-charge constraint is at its minimum, equivalently the series capacitor voltage around the outer loop is zero. This gives V_top=q0/(3C) across 2C and V_bottom=-q0/(3C) across C with consistent orientations. Represent the two post-switch oscillator currents as phasors: the common initial current components are equal and cancel in I_S, while the quadrature components from the initial capacitor voltages are V_top/(L omega) for the upper oscillator and V_bottom/(2L omega) for the lower oscillator. Project onto the differential coordinate I_S=i_upper-i_lower and take the phasor magnitude, obtaining I_max=|V_top/(L omega)-V_bottom/(2L omega)|=q0/sqrt(2LC).

图像描述：图中左侧是一条竖直支路，上、下两个电容串联，上方电容标为 2C，下方电容标为 C；上方 2C 旁标有上极板为 +、下极板为 -。右侧是一条竖直支路，上、下两个线圈串联，上方电感为 L，下方电感为 2L。左侧两个电容的中点与右侧两个电感的中点之间接有开关 S，图中开关初始断开。上下端导线分别把左、右支路的顶端和底端相连。

推理：开关断开时，两个电容之间的中点是孤立导体，其总电荷守恒。初态只有上方 2C 带电 q0，因此该中点上的电荷为 -q0。设在闭合 S 前、线圈电流达到最大时，上方电容 2C 的电压为 V_top，下方电容 C 的电压为 V_bottom，方向分别取为从上到下。此时电流最大，电场能在中点电荷守恒约束下最小，等价于外回路串联电容的总电压为零，所以 V_top+V_bottom=0。中点电荷为 -2C V_top + C V_bottom = -q0。联立得 V_top=q0/(3C)，V_bottom=-q0/(3C)。

闭合 S 后，图中上半部分形成 L 与 2C 的振荡支路，下半部分形成 2L 与 C 的振荡支路，二者 LC 乘积都为 2LC，因此共同角频率为 ω=1/sqrt(2LC)。闭合瞬间，由于原先两个电感串联，二者电流相等；这部分是共模电流，对开关电流相互抵消。只有由两个电容初始电压产生的差模电流贡献开关电流。用相量表示，上支路由初始电压产生的电流幅值为 V_top/(Lω)，下支路为 V_bottom/(2Lω)。若开关电流取差值，则其最大值为 |V_top/(Lω)-V_bottom/(2Lω)| = |q0/(3C Lω) - (-q0/(6C Lω))| = q0/(2CLω)。代入 ω=1/sqrt(2LC)，得到 I_max=q0/sqrt(2LC)。

闭合 S 后，图中上半部分形成 L 与 2C 的振荡支路，下半部分形成 2L 与 C 的振荡支路，二者 LC 乘积都为 2LC，因此共同角频率为 ω=1/sqrt(2LC)。闭合瞬间，由于原先两个电感串联，二者电流相等；这部分是共模电流，对开关电流相互抵消。只有由两个电容初始电压产生的差模电流贡献开关电流。用相量表示，上支路由初始电压产生的电流幅值为 V_top/(Lω)，下支路为 V_bottom/(2Lω)。若开关电流取差值，则其最大值为 |V_top/(Lω)-V_bottom/(2Lω)| = |q0/(3C Lω) - (-q0/(6C Lω))| = q0/(2CLω)。代入 ω=1/sqrt(2LC)，得到 I_max=q0/sqrt(2LC)。

raw_record.original_question: Initially, a switch $S$ is unshorted in the circuit shown in the figure on the right, a capacitor of capacitance $2C$ carries the electric charge $q_{0}$, a capacitor of capacitance $C$ is uncharged, and there are no electric currents in both coils of inductance $L$ and $2L$, respectively. The capacitor starts to discharge and at the moment when the current in the coils reaches its maximum value, the switch $S$ is instantly shorted. Find the maximum current $I_{\max}$ through the switch $S$ thereafter.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description first: The attached circuit diagram shows a rectangular circuit. The left vertical branch contains two capacitors in series: the upper capacitor is labeled 2C and has the indicated initial polarity + on its upper plate and - on its lower plate; the lower capacitor is labeled C. The right vertical branch contains two inductors in series: the upper one is labeled L and the lower one is labeled 2L. A switch S connects the midpoint between the two capacitors to the midpoint between the two inductors, and it is initially open.

Reasoning: With S open, the midpoint between the capacitors is isolated from the midpoint between the inductors, so the whole outer path is one series loop containing capacitors 2C and C and inductors L and 2L. Let V1 be the voltage across the 2C capacitor from top node to left midpoint, and V2 be the voltage across the C capacitor from left midpoint to bottom node.

Before the switch is closed, the net charge on the isolated left midpoint is conserved. Initially the lower plate of the 2C capacitor has charge -q0 and the upper plate of the C capacitor is uncharged, so the midpoint charge is -q0. Thus
-2C V1 + C V2 = -q0.
At the instant when the common series current is maximum, di/dt = 0, so the inductor voltages vanish. Therefore the two capacitor voltages around the outer loop cancel:
V1 + V2 = 0.
Solving gives
V1 = q0/(3C), V2 = -q0/(3C).

After S is closed, the circuit splits into two LC loops: an upper loop with 2C and L, and a lower loop with C and 2L. Their angular frequencies are equal:
ω = 1/sqrt(L·2C) = 1/sqrt(2L·C) = 1/sqrt(2LC).
The inductor currents are continuous at the instant of switching and are initially equal, so their common current part cancels in the switch current. The switch current is the difference between the two loop-current oscillations. Its sinusoidal amplitude is
| V1/(Lω) - V2/(2Lω) |
= | q0/(3C Lω) - (-q0/(3C·2Lω)) |
= q0/(2CLω).
Using ω = 1/sqrt(2LC), this becomes
Imax = q0/sqrt(2LC).
